subject: Objects
notes: Rule (9.3.6 match rule 4 d), cite.py OK 4) d)): a BY CONTENT parameter matches a non-index/object/pointer formal that 'may be a receiving data item in a MOVE statement with the parameter of the invocation as a sending data item'. The five MOVE-legal pairs refused before are admitted (w1006a, kb/Work PB1113; A1/A2 float by PB1114): A3 literal 123 into PIC ZZ9.99 -> [123.00], A4 literal 12 into PIC N(4) -> [12  ], A5 B"1" into PIC N(4) -> [1   ], plus the boolean expression and the signed literal into PIC X. The class-pointer leg (14.8.2.3.3 2), cite.py OK: 'the conformance rules shall be the same as if a SET statement were performed') now asks the WHOLE SET question, not its category screen alone (w1007b, kb/Work PB1063): OoConformance.ContentMismatch's pointer arm calls SetBinder.PointerAssignmentReason, the one 14.9.39.3 SR19/SR20/SR22 pair verdict SET Formats 8/9 also use.
